page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, providing 6 physical cores and 12 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) via hyperthreading. The server features 96 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Cache provisioning includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set support encompasses AVX, AVX-512, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. It includes no local attached storage and no integrated GPUs, relying on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

In benchmark testing, the instance displays modest single-core compute performance, placing in lower percentiles across single-threaded tests, including Geekbench single-core (930) and gzip compression throughput. Multi-core performance is balanced, achieving average tier results in stress-ng multi-core execution (8837.03), PassMark CPU score (10161.81), and Geekbench multi-core (4693). Uncached memory read and write bandwidth hover in the average range at 59.2 GB/sec and 49.35 GB/sec, respectively. While small-model 135M LLM prompt processing delivers average rates of 668.6 tokens/sec, medium-model 7B text generation drops into lower tiers. Network-bound workloads like static web serving also fall into lower performance brackets due to the 2 Gbps network ceiling.

The substantial memory footprint of 96 GB RAM relative to 12 vCPUs offers favorable resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications that do not demand high per-core single-thread speeds. Because single-thread processing and network speeds are constrained, the instance is best aligned with in-memory caching layers such as Redis—demonstrating 8.48 million SET operations per second in testing—as well as relational databases, staging environments, and batch processing tasks where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing throughput.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized x86_64 instance provisioned with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz across 6 physical cores and 12 dedicated vCPUs. Equipped with 96 GB of RAM, it supplies an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation along with a 35 MB L3 cache. The server lacks attached local storage and GPUs, operating with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface. Benchmark results indicate weak single-threaded compute and static web throughput, balanced by average multi-core execution and uncached memory bandwidth, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 10,161.81 and 8.48 million Redis SET operations per second. With high RAM density relative to vCPU count, this instance provides strong cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads like in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, and medium-scale data processing tasks that do not require high single-core execution speeds.
